title: the coronation planned
hook: the second book opens with an old king asking a hall full of people a question

segments.voice: Yesterday: Rama strung the bow and spared the sage, and the first book closed quietly at home. Your line was leave me my power to move.

Many people know how the second book of the Ramayana ends: a prince in clothes made of bark, walking into the forest with his wife and his brother. So notice how the Ayodhya Kanda begins. Not with a villain. Not with a quarrel. With an old man who loves his son, and a room full of people who love him too. For the next few weeks, almost everything turns on one family's household, and the first thing in it is good news.
screen: `BARK CLOTHES AND A FOREST: THE END.` → `THE BEGINNING: GOOD NEWS.` → `ONE FAMILY'S HOUSEHOLD.`

segments.voice: Dasharatha has ruled a long time, and he feels it. He loves all four of his sons, the text says, but Rama is the one the whole city talks about. Valmiki pauses to describe him, and one detail stands out. If someone does Rama a single kindness, he is pleased by it. If someone does him a hundred wrongs, he doesn't keep count. Generous memory is how Valmiki introduces the man about to lose everything. So the king makes a plan. He'll name Rama the yuvaraja, the young king, the heir who shares the rule while his father is still alive. He doesn't simply announce it. He calls an assembly: counselors, leading citizens, kings from the lands around. The text notes, a little pointedly, that in his hurry he didn't send for Janaka, Sita's father, or the king of Kekaya, Bharata's grandfather. I've carried this kingdom a long time, Dasharatha says. My body is tired. I want to put the weight on my eldest son. If you agree, tell me. If there's a better course, tell me that too. The hall answers with one roar of yes. And the old king tests them: why Rama, while I'm still ruling well? So they tell him. His truthfulness, his courage, his kindness to ordinary people, how he asks after their families and their fields when he comes back from a journey. The choice is public, and glad. That's why what happens next will hurt so much.
screen: `AN OLD KING, A LONG REIGN.` · `ONE KINDNESS KEPT, A HUNDRED WRONGS NOT.` · `THE KING ASKS THE ASSEMBLY.` · `WHY RAMA? THE PEOPLE ANSWER.` · then, large: `THE CHOICE IS PUBLIC, AND GLAD.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one kindness someone did for you this year, small or large, and let it be vivid: the place, the face, what they said. If a hurt from the same person or the same year crowds in, let it sit further back for now, and spend the rest of the sit with the kindness.
Yuvaraja, the young king who shares the rule while his father still reigns. Dasharatha proposes Rama for the title, and asks his assembly, which answers with joy.
Your line: he doesn't keep count. One kindness kept, a hundred wrongs let go. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Many Hindu families read the Ayodhya Kanda as the heart of the Ramayana, and Rama's habit of remembering kindness and forgetting wrongs is often quoted as a model of character.

original.note: Sanskrit yuvarāja: young king. the heir named while the father still reigns, the title Dasharatha means to give Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama is about to become king.
what it means: he's to be made yuvaraja, heir and co-ruler, while his father still reigns.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki notes that Janaka and the king of Kekaya weren't sent for, a small detail that later readers have taken as a hint of the king's haste.

chat.says: Did Dasharatha just announce that Rama would be his heir?
options: No. He asked an assembly, and they roared yes and listed Rama's good qualities.
No. He asked Vasishtha to choose among the four sons by drawing lots.
Yes. He named Rama heir quietly, and told no one outside the family.
